newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NORTHERN IRELAND SEEK CLARIFICATION ON ALBANIA MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORTHERN IRELAND SEEK CLARIFICATION ON ALBANIA MATCH.

text.p: Northern Ireland have asked FIFA to tell them by Tuesday if next month's World Cup qualifier against Albania will go ahead as planned.

The match, due to be played in Belfast on December 14, is in doubt after FIFA, world soccer's governing body, announced on Wednesday it was suspending Albania in response to a government purge of the national soccer association (AFA).
The game may now be re-scheduled for a later date.
"We have told FIFA we need to know if the fixture is going ahead by Tuesday at the latest, as that is when our squad is announced," Irish FA spokesman John Quinn said on Thursday.

"It is unusual for this type of thing to happen but until we know more about it we cannot react. We have just got to wait for FIFA to explain what happens next. Because of the proximity of the game we are anxious to hear from them."
FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said he was confident the problem could be resolved.

"The decision (to suspend Albania) was taken to protect the national federation in the face of political interference," he said. "They are suspended until further notice and are ineligible to play World Cup matches."
He said FIFA acted after Albania's Ministry of Education and Sport suspended AFA general secretary Eduard Dervishi and dissolved the association's executive committee.
After two games, Albania are bottom of group nine, which also includes Germany, Portugal, Armenia and Ukraine.
